title: Manchester skip firm ordered to stop activity as site investigated

evidence_packet.title: Manchester skip firm ordered to stop activity as site investigated
evidence_packet.lead: The land in Hyde does not have planning permission for waste transfer activity, the council says
evidence_packet.summary: The land in Hyde does not have planning permission for waste transfer activity, the council says
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A skip firm has been ordered to stop its activity after concerns over an unauthorised tip Land at the MD Waste Management Ltd site on Edward Street in Hyde, Tameside, where a huge pile of rubbish has appeared, does not have planning permission for waste transfer activity, authorities said The Environment Agency (EA), Tameside Council and Greater Manchester Police are working together to investigate and remove the waste from the land "Illegal waste harms local communities and the environment," a council spokesperson said. The BBC has contacted MD Waste Management Ltd for comment Tameside Council has served a Temporary Stop Notice requiring "the unauthorised use of the site" to stop while investigations are carried out The council said it was working with the landowner to ensure compliance with the notice and the removal of waste from the land

Whistl has applied to use 60 HGVs and 95 trailers at Astley Business Park in Tyldesley, Wigan, which has been dogged by noise complaints from local residents. The office of the Traffic Commissioner said 131 individuals from 96 homes near to the giant warehouse complex had valid objections. Whistl said it would take part in the inquiry and has been "working with local residents", who will also be able to speak at the hearing. The two-day inquiry will consider the Whistl application on 10 and 11 November. 'Towering warehouses' Whistl began trading at the warehouse site on 20 July after it agreed a 15-year lease. Many residents have gardens close to the 350,000 sq ft (33,000 sq m) logistics site and have criticised the huge scale and appearance of the "towering warehouses" and reported a "dreadful racket". In late August, Whistl ended overnight transport operations at the site after it admitted the noise had "had an impact on nearby residents". The company agreed to cease transport operations between midnight and 06:00 and introduce more noise mitigation measures. title: New Chinese garden to open at RHS Bridgewater in Salford

evidence_packet.title: New Chinese garden to open at RHS Bridgewater in Salford
evidence_packet.lead: The garden, built by specialist craftspeople from China and the UK, opens to visitors on Saturday
evidence_packet.summary: The garden, built by specialist craftspeople from China and the UK, opens to visitors on Saturday
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The centrepiece of what the RHS describes as Europe's largest and most authentic classical Chinese garden will open to visitors in Greater Manchester on Saturday after more than eight years in the making The Yangzhou Scholars' Garden at RHS Garden Bridgewater in Salford is the result of a collaboration between organisations in China, the RHS and Greater Manchester's Chinese community Specialist craftspeople from China used traditional techniques "rarely seen outside China" to create the garden, the RHS said Marcus Chilton-Jones, head of RHS Garden Bridgewater, described it as a "lasting symbol of friendship, cultural exchange and shared learning." More than 200 trees and 4000 perennials have been planted throughout the garden, chosen for their symbolism -with themes of good fortune, prosperity, health and love At the centre of the gardens are four interconnected pavilions, which surround a central courtyard and pond. Each pavilion is dedicated to one of the four traditional scholarly arts: chess, music, calligraphy and painting

title: M61 lorry oil spill closes motorway for hours

evidence_packet.title: M61 lorry oil spill closes motorway for hours
evidence_packet.lead: A section of the southbound M61 near Bolton was closed after the spillage on Thursday morning
evidence_packet.summary: A section of the southbound M61 near Bolton was closed after the spillage on Thursday morning
evidence_packet.evidence_text: M61 lorry oil spill closes motorway for hours - BBC News Image source, Google Image caption, The M61 Southbound was closed, with diversions put in place By Naj Modak North West Published 24 September 2026 A section of motorway was closed after a lorry left a "significant" oil spill across the carriageway. The southbound M61 in Greater Manchester was shut between Junction 4 near Bolton and Junction 2 while the road was cleared after the spill at about 08:20 BST. National Highways said the HGV spilled oil across two lanes, stretching for a distance of about 2km (1.2 mile). Drivers were urged to allow extra time for journeys with the clean-up expected to take several hours and the closure still remaining in place some time after 14:00 BST. Traffic officers were at the scene assisting with traffic management, while two road sweepers and a sander were sent to help clear the oil. Drivers travelling south were being diverted at Junction 4 along a signposted route. title: Cheshire's Tatton Park Apple Day cancelled after poor harvest

evidence_packet.title: Cheshire's Tatton Park Apple Day cancelled after poor harvest
evidence_packet.lead: It is the first time the event has been cancelled in 24 years
evidence_packet.summary: It is the first time the event has been cancelled in 24 years
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tatton Park's annual Apple Day has been cancelled for the first time in 24 years after extreme weather and increased pest activity left organisers short of fruit to share with visitors The event in Cheshire will not take place this October following a significantly reduced harvest from the estate's collection of about 300 apple and pear trees Head gardener Simon Tetlow said prolonged summer drought had created one of the most challenging growing seasons the team had experienced He said the cancellation highlighted the challenges climate change posed for sustainable fruit growing Head gardener Simon Tetlow said: "For 24 years, our orchards have provided the centrepiece for a fantastic tasting day to celebrate the start of autumn, but this year a combination of prolonged drought and unprecedented pest pressures has left us without enough fruit to share wit He said the gardening team was already adapting what crops were grown, where they were planted and cultivation methods to improve resilience in future seasons

title: Plane landed in Manchester with 'minutes of fuel' left during storm

evidence_packet.title: Plane landed in Manchester with 'minutes of fuel' left during storm
evidence_packet.lead: The jet carrying 177 people had about 1% of its fuel remaining after a series of diversions last year
evidence_packet.summary: The jet carrying 177 people had about 1% of its fuel remaining after a series of diversions last year
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A passenger jet carrying 171 people landed with about one per cent of its fuel remaining after severe weather and a series of diversions left it with only minutes to spare, an air safety report said The Boeing 737 had been due to fly from Pisa, Italy, to Prestwick, near Glasgow, on 3 October last year, before being diverted via Edinburgh and eventually landing in Manchester During Storm Amy, the aircraft encountered three separate wind shear events, a change in wind speed and direction at different heights, and a request to divert to Manchester was initially refused Manchester Airport said its policy was to accept diversion requests if the airport had the capacity to receive the aircraft A report by Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) found the flight, which was carrying 171 passengers and six crew members, encountered deteriorating weather conditions on its approach to Prestwick The crew abandoned two landing attempts after receiving wind shear warnings and sought to divert to Manchester

title: Roadworks to cause 'severe congestion' at M60 Simister Island junction

evidence_packet.title: Roadworks to cause 'severe congestion' at M60 Simister Island junction
evidence_packet.lead: Motorway users are warned of major disruption around Simister Island on the M60 in Bury
evidence_packet.summary: Motorway users are warned of major disruption around Simister Island on the M60 in Bury
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Motorists have been warned of widespread disruption as £300m of improvement work is set to begin across a stretch of Greater Manchester motorway Road closures, diversions and temporary speed limits will be in place at Simister Island in Bury from Saturday, as work begins on a £255m-£296m project at Junction 18 of the M60 The ring road will be closed in both directions between Junctions 17 and 18 over the course of two weekends - 26 September to 28 September and 10 October to 12 October National Highways has advised road users to expect "severe congestion" and to "avoid travelling" in the area during the weekend - adding "it's going to be busy" It said the scheme, which was given the green-light last year , will improve traffic flow, support future housing, employment and growth across the region "We understand the inconvenience this work will cause and would like to thank the local community, including road users, for their continued support and patience," project manager Nicola Eastwell said

title: Salford girl, 7, wins national Lowry art prize

evidence_packet.title: Salford girl, 7, wins national Lowry art prize
evidence_packet.lead: Mia says she is "really happy" to have her artwork on display in the Lowry museum
evidence_packet.summary: Mia says she is "really happy" to have her artwork on display in the Lowry museum
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A seven-year-old girl has won a national competition for her artwork which was inspired by LS Lowry Mia, of Salford, was picked as the winner from 600 entries to the 2026 Copley Prize, an annual art competition run by the Lowry theatre and gallery Her artwork, titled A Man Going To Work, is now hanging in the Andrew Law Galleries, alongside the famous paintings by Lowry himself, and will remain on display for the next 12 months Mia said: "I feel so happy that my work will be in a real art gallery." Every year primary school-aged children from across the UK are invited to submit artwork inspired by LS Lowry to Lowry's Copley Prize Mia's work was chosen as this year's overall winner by Alison and Noel Copley who are huge admirers of LS Lowry's work and long-standing supporters of the Lowry's programmes for children and young people

title: Wasp spider spotted in North West for first time, Chester Zoo says

evidence_packet.title: Wasp spider spotted in North West for first time, Chester Zoo says
evidence_packet.lead: Wasp spiders pose no threat to humans, despite their warning colours and size, Chester Zoo says
evidence_packet.summary: Wasp spiders pose no threat to humans, despite their warning colours and size, Chester Zoo says
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A brightly coloured wasp spider has reached the north-west of England for the first time, conservationists have said The large black and yellow spider was recorded during a survey on Chester Zoo's estate, with a zoo spokesperson saying this was "the first time this fascinating mimic has reached the area" Wasp spiders have only previously been spotted in the south of England but zoo bosses believe this arrival, who they have nicknamed Wendy, is a sign that climate change was impacting UK wildlife A zoo spokesperson said: "Despite their warning colours and size, wasp spiders pose no threat to humans." Zoo conservationists said the wasp spider's discovery highlighted the need to make space for nature The discovery was made by Chester Zoo conservationists working with RECORD, Cheshire's local environmental records centre, and was subsequently confirmed by an expert from the British Arachnological Society, the zoo said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The centrepiece of what the RHS describes as Europe's largest and most authentic classical Chinese garden will open to visitors in Greater Manchester on Saturday after more than eight years in the making The Yangzhou Scholars' Garden at RHS Garden Bridgewater in Salford is the result of a collaboration between organisations in China, the RHS and Greater Manchester's Chinese community Specialist craftspeople from China used traditional techniques "rarely seen outside China" to create the garden, the RHS said Marcus Chilton-Jones, head of RHS Garden Bridgewater, described it as a "lasting symbol of friendship, cultural exchange and shared learning." More than 200 trees and 4000 perennials have been planted throughout the garden, chosen for their symbolism -with themes of good fortune, prosperity, health and love At the centre of the gardens are four interconnected pavilions, which surround a central courtyard and pond. Each pavilion is dedicated to one of the four traditional scholarly arts: chess, music, calligraphy and painting

evidence_packet.summary: A passenger jet carrying 171 people landed with about one per cent of its fuel remaining after severe weather and a series of diversions left it with only minutes to spare, an air safety report said The Boeing 737 had been due to fly from Pisa, Italy, to Prestwick, near Glasgow
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A passenger jet carrying 171 people landed with about one per cent of its fuel remaining after severe weather and a series of diversions left it with only minutes to spare, an air safety report said The Boeing 737 had been due to fly from Pisa, Italy, to Prestwick, near Glasgow, on 3 October last year, before being diverted via Edinburgh and eventually landing in Manchester During Storm Amy, the aircraft encountered three separate wind shear events, a change in wind speed and direction at different heights, and a request to divert to Manchester was initially refused Manchester Airport said its policy was to accept diversion requests if the airport had the capacity to receive the aircraft A report by Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) found the flight, which was carrying 171 passengers and six crew members, encountered deteriorating weather conditions on its approach to Prestwick The crew abandoned two landing attempts after receiving wind shear warnings and sought to divert to Manchester

evidence_packet.summary: The route has been revised of a proposed gas pipeline that would see compressed carbon dioxide stored under the sea in a project dubbed dangerous and potentially devastating to the countryside Peak Cluster, a joint initiative between four cement firms, said the changes followed c
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The route has been revised of a proposed gas pipeline that would see compressed carbon dioxide stored under the sea in a project dubbed dangerous and potentially devastating to the countryside Peak Cluster, a joint initiative between four cement firms, said the changes followed consultation and technical assessments Two arms would begin near Hope, Derbyshire and Cauldon, Staffordshire, joining together near Marton in Cheshire before heading to Hoylake on the Wirral The £5bn government-backed scheme features a buried pipeline as well as above-ground installations, but people living along its route are unhappy, and one councillor has described it as a "dangerous, dangerous thing" As well as altering its course in some areas, the proposals have reduced the width of the route earmarked of the pipeline from 300m (328 yards) to approximately 100m (109 yards) The new plans will be the subject of consultations in Staffordshire, Derbyshire and Cheshire in November, with the proposals for the Wirral due to be the focus in January

evidence_packet.evidence_text: In fact one youth worker says children and young people have so few qualms about dealing with AI that chatbots have become ‘trusted adults’ Glyn Potts says teenagers will consult AI characters on everything from homework to bullying. And that’s a particular concern in a world where teachers and professionals are becoming further removed from the digital world of children “The concern from me is that we are being outpaced by AI and social media as we try to use it as an asset,” says Glyn, a former headteacher and now CEO of Greater Manchester Youth Federation He is worried that young people no longer have the support they once had in school as an unintended consequence of the phone ban. Instead they are forming ‘friendships’ with chatbots and turning to AI as a trusted confidant View 6 Images "Whether it’s researching homework with ChatGPT or making friends with a fictional persona on Character.ai, they are increasingly becoming a part of children's lives." The truth was so much worse Nicola Clarke was jailed earlier this year View Image Nicola Clarke (Image: Greater Manchester Police) Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:12, 25 Sep 2026 Updated 07:01, 25 Sep 2026 A woman jailed after she was caught red-handed after 11 years of stealing from her own bosses has been hauled back into court Nicola Clarke, 56, was a top accountant for Business Computer Projects Ltd. She ended up becoming their head of accounts, and held sole responsibility for all the financial aspects of the company, Minshull Street Crown Court heard in February this year However, from 2008, she abused her position to steal from them in three 'discreet' ways; by claiming unauthorised overtime payments, stealing petty cash and unauthorised use of the company's credit card The total loss to the company was £128,352, the court heard. The fraud was revealed in June 2019 when it was discovered Clarke had been using the credit card. She claimed the fraud had been going on for six months, when in fact it had actually been taking place over 11 years An investigation revealed the full extent of Clarke's dishonesty. She pleaded guilty to three charges of fraud by abuse of position and was jailed for 18 months

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fuel Prices Diesel prices hit over £2 a litre in Greater Manchester petrol stations amid fears over Donald Trump ban At one service station in our region, it is now almost £2.20p per litre Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 20:32, 24 Sep 2026 Diesel prices have risen above £2 per litre at a number of Greater Manchester petrol stations as nationwide prices reach a near record high. It comes amid fears Donald Trump will ban US diesel exports in a bid to ease prices for American drivers The average price of diesel in the UK is currently 197.75p per litre, according to the RAC's Fuel Watch, where the data is updated daily. That is just short of the record average high of 199.07p per litre in July 2022, which was set following Russia's invasion of Ukraine However, the RAC says diesel at motorway services is currently costing 214.4p per litre. And the prices at a number of filling stations in Greater Manchester are now above £2 View 3 Images The Shell on Barlow Moor Road in Chorlton on Thursday (Image: Manchester Evening News) At Birch services on the M62 near Rochdale , diesel is currently almost £2.20 a litre, at 219.2p, according to Fuel Finder. title: Ryebank Fields campaigners score first victory but the clock is ticking

evidence_packet.title: Ryebank Fields campaigners score first victory but the clock is ticking
evidence_packet.lead: Trafford Ryebank Fields campaigners score first victory but the clock is ticking Controversial plans could see homes built on the community space Comments News Hannah Richardson 12:30, 24 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Save Ryebank Fields campaigners gathered Campaigners against a contro
evidence_packet.summary: Trafford Ryebank Fields campaigners score first victory but the clock is ticking Controversial plans could see homes built on the community space Comments News Hannah Richardson 12:30, 24 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Save Ryebank Fields campaigners gathered Campaigners against a contro
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Ryebank Fields campaigners score first victory but the clock is ticking Controversial plans could see homes built on the community space Comments News Hannah Richardson 12:30, 24 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Save Ryebank Fields campaigners gathered Campaigners against a controversial plan to build on a much-loved community space scored their first victory as Trafford councillors defied planning advice A unanimous vote by members of the planning committee on Tuesday night (September 22) saw proposals to hand decision-making power to Manchester City Council roundly rejected. A plan for 120 new homes on Ryebank Fields would see a new access road created from Rye Bank Road, within Officers had told the committee they believed the scheme should be decided as a whole and, as the majority of the land is within Manchester, that decision would be better coming from the city council . This would reduce the risk of the scheme being decided on a ‘salami slice’ bas However, councillors said they did not believe giving up their right to decide the scheme was in the best interest of their residents. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts She told bosses it had been going on six months. The truth was so much worse Nicola Clarke was jailed earlier this year View Image Nicola Clarke (Image: Greater Manchester Police) Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:12, 25 Sep 2026 Updated 07:01, 25 Sep 2026 A woman jailed after she was caught red-handed after 11 years of stealing from her own bosses has been hauled back into court Nicola Clarke, 56, was a top accountant for Business Computer Projects Ltd. She ended up becoming their head of accounts, and held sole responsibility for all the financial aspects of the company, Minshull Street Crown Court heard in February this year However, from 2008, she abused her position to steal from them in three 'discreet' ways; by claiming unauthorised overtime payments, stealing petty cash and unauthorised use of the company's credit card The total loss to the company was £128,352, the court heard. The fraud was revealed in June 2019 when it was discovered Clarke had been using the credit card. She claimed the fraud had been going on for six months, when in fact it had actually been taking place over 11 years An investigation revealed the full extent of Clarke's dishonesty. She pleaded guilty to three charges of fraud by abuse of position and was jailed for 18 months

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fuel Prices Diesel prices hit over £2 a litre in Greater Manchester petrol stations amid fears over Donald Trump ban At one service station in our region, it is now almost £2.20p per litre Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 20:32, 24 Sep 2026 Diesel prices have risen above £2 per litre at a number of Greater Manchester petrol stations as nationwide prices reach a near record high. It comes amid fears Donald Trump will ban US diesel exports in a bid to ease prices for American drivers The average price of diesel in the UK is currently 197.75p per litre, according to the RAC's Fuel Watch, where the data is updated daily. That is just short of the record average high of 199.07p per litre in July 2022, which was set following Russia's invasion of Ukraine However, the RAC says diesel at motorway services is currently costing 214.4p per litre. And the prices at a number of filling stations in Greater Manchester are now above £2 View 3 Images The Shell on Barlow Moor Road in Chorlton on Thursday (Image: Manchester Evening News) At Birch services on the M62 near Rochdale , diesel is currently almost £2.20 a litre, at 219.2p, according to Fuel Finder. evidence_packet.evidence_text: In fact one youth worker says children and young people have so few qualms about dealing with AI that chatbots have become ‘trusted adults’ Glyn Potts says teenagers will consult AI characters on everything from homework to bullying. And that’s a particular concern in a world where teachers and professionals are becoming further removed from the digital world of children “The concern from me is that we are being outpaced by AI and social media as we try to use it as an asset,” says Glyn, a former headteacher and now CEO of Greater Manchester Youth Federation He is worried that young people no longer have the support they once had in school as an unintended consequence of the phone ban. Instead they are forming ‘friendships’ with chatbots and turning to AI as a trusted confidant View 6 Images "Whether it’s researching homework with ChatGPT or making friends with a fictional persona on Character.ai, they are increasingly becoming a part of children's lives." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester 'In 2026 in modern Britain, you shouldn’t feel afraid just for going to pray' Two arrests were made in the city by anti-terror police on Sunday linked to an alleged threat to the Jewish community Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy repo Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig said anti-terror arrests made in the city connected with an alleged threat to the Jewish community ‘sent a chill down my spine’ Counter terror cops from the Metropolitan Police descended on Newton Street in the Northern Quarter at 2.34pm on Sunday (September 20), arresting two men on suspicion of terrorism That action was followed by a second swoop at a hostel on Lancaster Road in Salford and a raid on a flat in Liverpool. The mayor added: “It sent a chill down my spine that a year on from the evil terrorist attack in Heaton Park synagogue, our Jewish communities were facing t “The fact that they find themselves in this situation will no doubt be worrying them.”

evidence_packet.summary: Salford Salford Council doubled number of parking fines last year, and these are the three hotspots The local authority issued more than 40,000 PCNs News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 17:26, 24 Sep 2026 View 3 Images (Image: Copyright Unknow Salford Council doubled down
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Salford Council doubled number of parking fines last year, and these are the three hotspots The local authority issued more than 40,000 PCNs News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 17:26, 24 Sep 2026 View 3 Images (Image: Copyright Unknow Salford Council doubled down on parking tickets in 2025 in a crackdown aimed to raise cash. The authority slapped motorists with nearly 40,000 Penalty Charge Notices (PCNs) last year – up from just over 20,000 in 2024 The stark increase came after council bosses warned they would use tougher parking enforcement to grow the council’s revenue. In 2025, the local authority issued 39,365 PCNs compared to 20,874 the previous year. The fines raked in £2,619,450 over the course of 2025 – almost doubl A freedom of information request submitted by the local democracy reporting service also revealed the three worst roads where Salford drivers are receiving the most fines View 3 Images 1,330 drivers were fined on Ordsall Lane (Image: Copyright Unknown) Ordsall Lane between the busy Trafford Road and Regent Road, was named the worst for parking issues in the city. The council issued 1,330 fines – and made £84,500 – on the road, which has double yellows and strict parking conditions

evidence_packet.evidence_text: M61 LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 15 hours ago M61 traffic RECAP as motorway shuts for HOURS with massive delays after lorry fire Miles of congestion built up after the incident on the M61 motorway Traffic on the M61 motorway ( Image: Facebook ) News Ashli A stretch of the motorway is was shut following the incident on Thursday morning (September 24). It was closed between junction four for the A6 at Farnworth to junction three for the M60 National Highways said a closure was in place following a lorry fire and oil spillage that would remain in place for 'several hours' A diversion route was put in place with delays of over 30 minutes as of 11.45am. In a statement, National Highways said: "The M61 in Greater Manchester is closed southbound between J4 (M60/ A666) near Bolton and J2 due to a lorry fire and oil spillage "National Highways Traffic Officers are in attendance assisting with traffic management. The vehicle involved has been recovered however there is an extensive oil spillage across lanes 1 and 2 of the carriageway "Two sweepers and a sander have been requested to scene to assist with clearing the spillage. The closure is expected to remain in place for several hours."

Its draft local plan identifies the main areas where up to 14,052 new homes and a minimum of 135,099 sq m of industrial space is to be built before 2042 Health Innovation Bolton (HIB) is the largest site earmarked to be taken out of the green belt. It is a large area of land between Royal Bolton Hospital and the M61 where it is proposed 1,895 homes and 40,839 sq ft of employment space will be created Another current green belt area within the draft plans is described as the Blackrod employment cluster, which is green land close to the village’s railway station. It is allocated for 44,800 sq m of employment space The third potential area of green belt to disappear is an extension to the Logistics North industrial park, just off the M61, near Over Hulton. That would accommodate between 30,000 to 80,000 sq m of employment space and possibly some housing A council cabinet report states that there are ‘two mixed use sites’ in the plan. Justice has caught up with Peter Garns, 69, who police said used a 'false pretext of love and care' to target the vulnerable youngster in Stockport Garns was found guilty by a jury after a trial of seven counts of indecent assault and one count of unlawful sexual intercourse. Police said the charges he was convicted of related to the same girl over a three-year period in the late 1990s and early 2000s Detectives, speaking after a sentencing hearing, said Garns, of no fixed abode, groomed her by giving her cigarettes and putting credit onto her mobile phone At Bolton Crown Court on Monday (September 21), he was jailed for sixteen-and-a-half years "Garns manipulated the girl into believing they had a genuine relationship and that he loved her," said a GMP spokesperson after the hearing

evidence_packet.lead: Manchester Airport Ryanair flight issues urgent 'Mayday' alert before Manchester Airport landing in serious incident The Ryanair flight with 171 passengers on board touched down at Manchester Airport 'with a fuel quantity significantly below the final The pilots of a Ryanair flig
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester Airport Ryanair flight issues urgent 'Mayday' alert before Manchester Airport landing in serious incident The Ryanair flight with 171 passengers on board touched down at Manchester Airport 'with a fuel quantity significantly below the final The pilots of a Ryanair flig
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Ryanair flight issues urgent 'Mayday' alert before Manchester Airport landing in serious incident The Ryanair flight with 171 passengers on board touched down at Manchester Airport 'with a fuel quantity significantly below the final The pilots of a Ryanair flight with 171 passengers on board declared a 'MAYDAY' alert for low fuel before touching down at Manchester Airport after three aborted landings at two other airports, a new report reveals The flight - which was caught up in Storm Amy in October last year - finally landed at Manchester 'with a fuel quantity significantly below the final reserve fuel', adds the report It says the pilots were 'increasingly concerned' about the level of fuel and the third failed landing prompted the declaration of a 'MAYDAY, MAYDAY, MAYDAY, MAYDAY FUEL' alert to air traffic control - and the 'request for an immediate diversion to Manchester' "There was no further discussion by the pilots about the expected fuel remaining on arrival at Manchester, except that they realised they would not have enough fuel for another go-around," says the report compiled after an investigation. An earlier request to divert to Manchester Following what was described as a 'serious incident', a report by the Air Accident Investigation Branch (AAIB) into what happened has now been published

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Ryebank Fields campaigners score first victory but the clock is ticking Controversial plans could see homes built on the community space Comments News Hannah Richardson 12:30, 24 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Save Ryebank Fields campaigners gathered Campaigners against a controversial plan to build on a much-loved community space scored their first victory as Trafford councillors defied planning advice A unanimous vote by members of the planning committee on Tuesday night (September 22) saw proposals to hand decision-making power to Manchester City Council roundly rejected. A plan for 120 new homes on Ryebank Fields would see a new access road created from Rye Bank Road, within Officers had told the committee they believed the scheme should be decided as a whole and, as the majority of the land is within Manchester, that decision would be better coming from the city council . This would reduce the risk of the scheme being decided on a ‘salami slice’ bas However, councillors said they did not believe giving up their right to decide the scheme was in the best interest of their residents. The decision was met with loud applause from those watching in the public gallery Thousands of residents, along with Stretford and Urmston MP Andrew Western, had called on the council to keep that decision in-house

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A pair of giant lungs made up of iconic North West landmarks appeared in Manchester yesterday to highlight the shocking number of people affected by lung cancer across the region In the North West, lung cancer is 25% more common when compared with the rest of England, according to newly available data analysed by North West Cancer Research It is this stark figure that is behind the latest campaign from the charity. In Plain Sight highlights the most common symptoms of the condition which can often go ignored or, in some cases, mistaken for something less serious Breathlessness, coughing up blood, ongoing tiredness, or a cough lasting more than three weeks are all warning signs of lung cancer, while unexplained weight loss, and aches and pains can also be symptoms to look out for As part of the campaign launch, North West Cancer Research created a nine-foot-tall installation featuring a pair of lungs at a community centre in Hulme, with local people invited to come along and find out more At first glance, they look like an ordinary set of lungs and trachea. But upon closer inspection, it is possible to spot iconic landmarks from across the North West, from The Blackpool Tower to Liverpool Lime Street and Manchester’s Beetham Tower

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police who have been leading an investigation into human remains found close to the M67 in Tameside, can now confirm the identity of the person who was found under the bridge in August After a forensic post-mortem was carried out, and a bone was sent for examination. DNA was extracted from the bone, and the remains were identified as 41-year-old Ajani Campbell, from Preston in Lancashire Enquiries showed that Ajani was circulated as a high-risk missing person after he left his home address on Saturday 24 January 2026 It was also established that he boarded a train in Preston on that same day and travelled to Manchester Piccadilly. Train station footage captures him walking through the station at 12.30am on Sunday 25 January 2026 He is then tracked into the city centre and captured on CCTV footage at 1.48am on Deansgate at the junction with Quay Street. This was the last confirmed sighting of Ajani Ajani’s family have paid tribute to him below

title: 'The mystery we all want solved': what's with all the corn on Market Street?

evidence_packet.title: 'The mystery we all want solved': what's with all the corn on Market Street?
evidence_packet.lead: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred van
evidence_packet.summary: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred van
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred vans, and the doors swing open. Out from within comes cart after cart full of corn This is the not-entirely-secret HQ of the Market Street corn vendors: a four-storey council-owned car park, sitting across two of Manchester’s busiest streets. When I get there, the men are working in silence, hands sheathed in black gloves, bags of sweetcorn torn open, cardboard Just as I’m about to approach a vendor, I’m forwarded an email from a reader. It has the subject line The Mystery We All Want Solved "The reason I’m writing is because the people of Manchester are desperate to know what the hell is going on with all of the corn sellers on Market St "Why are there now so many of them? How on earth do they make a profit? Are they independent vendors or all part of the same company? Is their presence legal? What does their proliferation say about the state of the city centre?”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The situation has prompted concern that people are being deterred from visiting local high streets Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Cash payments have been suspended at a number of pay-and-display machines across Altrincham and Hale after what Trafford Council has described as a sustained campaign of vandalism Notices have appeared on numerous machines in recent days informing motorists that cash payments are unavailable and advising them to pay using the RingGo app Trafford Council says a “significant number” of its machines have been put out of action by targeted criminal damage and that it is working with Greater Manchester Police to identify those responsible But the situation has prompted concern that people who cannot or do not want to use smartphone payments are being deterred from visiting local high streets – with particular concerns raised about older and vulnerable residents Hale Civic Society said Cecil Road car park was “noticeably quiet” when members visited at 11.30am today and questioned whether the problems with the machines were contributing to the lack of cars

evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Council has approved a new package of interim governance arrangements
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council has approved a new package of interim governance arrangements. These measures are designed to strengthen democratic oversight, provide clear political leadership across key service areas and support transparent decision-making while the borough continues to work towards the appointment of a Council Leader and Cabinet. The arrangements were approved by Council on 16 September and include the creation of interim Lead Member and Deputy Lead Member roles aligned to the Council's four directorates. The arrangements form part of a wider governance framework developed following legal advice, engagement with the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, and discussions between political group leaders. Under the arrangements, Chief Executive Shelley Kipling will continue to exercise delegated executive powers, while Lead Members provide political oversight, advocacy and a visible link between residents, councillors and services. The roles carry no executive decision-making powers. The four Interim Lead Member portfolios have been allocated to the Council's four largest political groups, with deputy roles assigned from the same groups. Interim Lead Member appointments Resources - Lead Member: Sam Al-Hamdani (Liberal Democrats) - Deputy Lead Member: Mark Kenyon (Liberal Democrats) The Resources portfolio will provide political oversight of the Council's finances, budget management, transformation programme, corporate services, governance, workforce and organisational performance. Place - Lead Member: Arooj Shah (Labour) - Deputy Lead Member: Elaine Taylor (Labour) The Place portfolio will focus on regeneration, economic growth, planning, housing, highways, environmental services, transport and the continued delivery of major projects that support Oldham

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge. Council officers first visited the site on Thursday 6th August following concerns from residents and people using the park. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August. As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their vehicles and belongings. The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime. After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment. The site was vacated later that day. A significant amount of waste was left behind, which has now been removed by the Council’s cleansing team. A Council spokesperson said: “We understand the concerns raised by residents and people using Oldham Edge, and we thank them for their patience while we followed the legal process. “We always try to resolve unauthorised encampments through discussion and voluntary cooperation wherever possible. However, when the site was not vacated as agreed, it became necessary to take further action. “We worked closely with Greater Manchester Police throughout to make sure the situation was handled lawfully and proportionately. “The encampment has now left and our cleansing team has completed the clean-up, allowing the area to be returned to the local community.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sat 26th Sep, 2026 - Sankeys Sankeys re-opening party with Low Steppa Sankeys, Sidney St, Manchester M1 7HB Sat 26th Sep, 2026 Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Sankeys Manchester kicks off its Autumn/Winter season on Saturday 26 September, returning to its new permanent home on Sidney Street with Low Steppa, Pirate Copy and Mike Morrisey B2B Luca606 taking over the opening party It marks the start of the club’s first full season back in Manchester since its much-loved Ancoats venue closed in 2017. The new 500-capacity space keeps the stripped-back, music-first approach Sankeys built its name on, but arrives this autumn with a few changes behind the scene Carved out of the former green room, Room 2 is a smaller, clandestine space designed for close-up sets and a slightly different pace from the main room. Moving the artist dressing rooms upstairs has opened up more space downstairs too, while the club’s LED matrix installation ret The music remains firmly rooted in underground house, with Sankeys deliberately keeping much of its weekly programming under wraps until closer to each event. After the opening party, the season will bring the likes of Arapu, George Smeddles, Paisley Jensen, Richy Ahmed, Darius S There’s also a Seb Zito B2B Rossko set among the dates lined up between September and mid-December, with further special guests still to be announced

A-Kin founded by long-time friends Gasim and Sean, have become one of the city’s most exciting supper club names, turning dinners into nights built around food, music and conversation. Portfolio brings Julian Pizer back to the grills Tartuffe , as ever, will be holding the whole thing together from the grills, starting with oysters and venison, bringing in a seasonal nectarine gazpacho, and finishing their side of the menu with Alp Blossom cheese and elderberry honey before Kallos take things into dessert Tartuffe start things off with an oyster dressed with beef fat, wasabi and XO. It’s already something of a house classic, and won Best Dressed Oyster at Manchester Oyster Festival 2026. The beef fat comes from Cheshire cattle, aged and smoked before being worked into the dish

S.A.S.S., the four-way team-up of Saoirse, Moxie, Peach and Shanti Celeste, will The party takes over the full Depot Mayfield site, with music spread across Depot, Concourse, Archive, the Star & Garter and a brand new 1,000-capacity Vault stage curated by Glasgow queer club night Ponyboy. The new space will host Lady Shaka, Armana Khan, Meg10 b2b Luca Eck, I. There’s also a major nod to Manchester club history, with Homobloc celebrating 35 years of FLESH, the pioneering LGBTQ+ night launched at The Haçienda. Tim Lennox, Kath McDermott, Guy Williams, DJ Paulette and Mike Hux will take over the upstairs of the Star & Garter, alongside a Away from the decks, more than 150 Homodolls will appear throughout the venue with drag, dance, theatre, pole and immersive performance, including Club Rat’s PU RAUL’S SUPERMODELS, The Strippers of MCR, Blackstage Pole and a new FLINTA-focused work from Maisha Kungu Dance

evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
evidence_packet.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Digital’s MD Future 26 conference brought together industry leaders, academia, founders, investors and policymakers, to look at the businesses and technologies shaping the next phase of the region’s tech economy Held at Campfield Studios, the newly restored former Victorian produce and exhibition hall, which was completed at the end of the city’s Industrial Revolution, the venue offered a striking backdrop for discussions about Manchester’s role in today’s AI and digital transformation Across a day covering physical AI, infrastructure, cyber security, health, space and quantum, some clear themes came through. The next phase of AI is likely to be much less about what a model can demonstrate on a screen and much more about whether businesses can deploy it securel There is also an opportunity for Manchester and the wider North that goes beyond simply increasing AI adoption. The region already has strengths across advanced materials, computing infrastructure, cyber security, health innovation and emerging technologies such as quantum. The c The previous day also saw an Innovation Day, where 20 of the region’s most innovative startups pitched to the biggest organisations working across defence, national security and technology, then took part in a number of Round Table discussions Here’s our write up of the full day’s conference

The partnership aims to lower entry barriers for scaling businesses by providing reciprocal workspace access, market entry support, and cross-border network integration across two of Europe’s most dynamic technology hubs. Key features of the agreement include: Market Entry and Connections: Broadening connections to help startups access new markets, including launch events for new residents taking up permanent space and network access. Reciprocal Desk Access: Providing founders with a base to expand internationally and grow their presence in Manchester and Dublin with low to no overheads. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. The position was one targeted by United in the summer window While the priority was to strengthen the midfield, the final days and weeks of the window saw them try to add to their left-back options. They eventually decided to go with what they have for the first half of the season With Michael Carrick seemingly preferring to play Patrick Dorgu further forward, it leaves Luke Shaw as the only natural senior left-back in the squad. While he played every Premier League game last season, he has had previous spells out due to injury Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News! A recent injury to Shaw has led to Dorgu playing further back as he provided cover. However, United could look to provide genuine competition to the 31-year-old when the window reopens in January

Here's everything you can expect at M What's On Dianne Bourne Lifestyle Editor 19:14, 23 Sep 2026 Updated 07:27, 24 Sep 2026 A huge new entertainment district for Manchester has been officially unveiled next to Manchester City's Etihad Stadium - with the £300million Medlock Square packed with restaurants, bars, a hot As well as the huge new hotel, The Medlock by Radisson Blu , which opened at the start of the month, there are now the first restaurant and bar openings, with more to follow next week and in the run up to Christmas . There will also be a spectacular new sky-walk attraction above Bosses say the £300m development marks a "significant new chapter in East Manchester's continued investment and transformation overseen by City Football Group since 2008". Developed as a 365-day destination, Medlock Square forms part of the wider evolution of the Etihad Campus in The scale of the development will have a significant impact beyond Medlock Square itself.
